title: 634. Joan of Arc: Heroine in Chains (Part 3)

sentences.en: I went to her lodging to see her, and she sent for wine, and she told me that we would soon drink wine in Paris.
sentences.zh: 我到她住处去见她，她叫人拿来酒，并告诉我，我们很快就能在巴黎共饮美酒了。

sentences.en: It seemed to me a gift from heaven that she was there, and that I was seeing and hearing her.
sentences.zh: 她能在那里，而我能亲眼见到她、亲耳听到她说话，这对我来说简直是上天的恩赐。

sentences.en: She left cells on Monday at the hour of Vespers, alongside a great body of armed men.
sentences.zh: 周一晚祷时分，她在一大群武装人员的簇拥下离开了修道院。

sentences.en: I saw her mount her horse, arrayed all in white armour, with only her head bare and holding a small axe.
sentences.zh: 我看见她骑上马，身披白甲，只露出头部，手里拿着一把小斧头。

sentences.en: The great black charger was very restive at her door, and would not let her mount.
sentences.zh: 那匹高大的黑马在门前显得非常不安，不肯让她骑上去。

sentences.en: Lead him, she said, to the cross which is in front of the church.
sentences.zh: 她说：“把它牵到教堂前面的十字架那里去。”

sentences.en: And there she mounted, the horse standing still, as if he had been bound.
sentences.zh: 她在那儿上了马，马儿站着不动，仿佛被拴住了一样。

sentences.en: Then, turning towards the church which was close by, she said in a beautiful feminine voice, You priests and people of the church, make processions and prayers to God for us.
sentences.zh: 随后，她转向旁边的教堂，用优美而柔和的女性嗓音说道：“你们这些教堂的神职人员和信众，请为我们举行游行，向上帝祈祷吧。”

sentences.en: Then, turning to the road,
sentences.zh: 接着，她转向大路，

sentences.en: Forward!
sentences.zh: “前进！”

sentences.en: Forward!
sentences.zh: “前进！”

sentences.en: She said.
sentences.zh: 她喊道。

sentences.en: Her unfolded standard was carried by a page.
sentences.zh: 她的旗帜由一名侍从展开并高举着。

sentences.en: She had her small axe in her hand, and by her side rode a brother, who had joined her eight days before.
sentences.zh: 她手里拿着那把小斧头，身边骑着一位八天前刚加入她队伍的修士。

sentences.en: So, that's a letter written on the 8th of June, 1429, by a soft, tender-hearted young nobleman, Guy de Laval.
sentences.zh: 所以，这是一封写于1429年6月8日的信，出自一位温柔、心肠柔软的年轻贵族盖伊·德·拉瓦尔之手。

sentences.en: He's writing to his mother, and he is pumped.
sentences.zh: 他正在写信给母亲，而且他非常兴奋。

sentences.en: He is so full of excitement, because he has just seen the heroine of the hour, Joan of Arc.
sentences.zh: 他激动万分，因为他刚刚见到了当下的女英雄——圣女贞德。

sentences.en: And Dominic, how beautifully you conveyed her feminine voice there.
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，你刚才传达出的那种女性嗓音真是太美妙了。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: I'm glad you enjoyed that.
sentences.zh: 很高兴你喜欢。

sentences.en: As though she'd been brought back to life.
sentences.zh: 就好像她死而复生了一样。

sentences.en: So, a month has gone by since this extraordinary moment in the history of France and French military achievements, the liberation of Orléans.
sentences.zh: 距离法国历史上这一非凡时刻——奥尔良之围的解除，已经过去一个月了。

sentences.en: So, to remind listeners, Orléans had been under siege for six months by the English.
sentences.zh: 提醒一下听众，奥尔良当时已经被英国人围困了六个月。

sentences.en: It had been on the verge, it seemed, of surrender.
sentences.zh: 看起来，它已经到了投降的边缘。

sentences.en: Had the English taken it, they would have been able to cross the River Loire and advance deep into south-central France.
sentences.zh: 如果英国人攻占了它，他们就能跨过卢瓦尔河，深入法国中南部。

sentences.en: But, in the nick of time, the siege had been broken, the English had been driven back, and the banner of the House of Valois, the ancient line of French kings,
sentences.zh: 但就在千钧一发之际，围城被打破，英国人被击退，瓦卢瓦家族——法国古老王室的旗帜，

sentences.en: still flies over Orléans.
sentences.zh: 依然在奥尔良上空飘扬。

sentences.en: So, Tom, various people have taken some credit for this achievement, and you can take us through them.
sentences.zh: 那么，汤姆，不同的人都对这一成就贡献了力量，你可以带我们了解一下他们吗？

sentences.en: But, of course, one above all is the subject of this podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 当然，其中最重要的一位正是我们这期播客的主题。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So, various French captains, as you said, had definitely played their part in this great drama.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，几位法国将领确实在这场大戏中发挥了各自的作用。

sentences.en: So, there was Jean, the Bastard of Orléans, illegitimate half-brother of the wretched Duke of Orléans, who was languishing in the Tower of London,
sentences.zh: 比如奥尔良的私生子让，他是那位被囚禁在伦敦塔中、郁郁寡欢的奥尔良公爵的同父异母兄弟，

sentences.en: had been there ever since the Battle of Agincourt, where he'd been captured.
sentences.zh: 自阿金库尔战役被俘后，他就一直被关在那里。

sentences.en: You know, he is, his team, Orléans, on the scene, very battle-hardened, very shrewd, very well-connected, despite the fact he's illegitimate.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他和他的人马就在奥尔良现场，久经沙场，非常精明，人脉极广，尽管他是私生子。

sentences.en: He's cousin to the French king, to Charles VII.
sentences.zh: 他是法国国王查理七世的表亲。

sentences.en: Then there's Etienne de Vigneault, better known as Laire, the Wrath of God, a man of very humble origins, had his legs crushed by a chimney of a pub falling on top of it,
sentences.zh: 还有艾蒂安·德·维尼奥勒，也就是更广为人知的“拉伊尔”，人称“上帝之怒”，出身卑微，曾因酒馆烟囱倒塌压碎了双腿，

sentences.en: but still very feared, very charismatic, the great warlord of his day.
sentences.zh: 但他依然令人畏惧，极具个人魅力，是那个时代伟大的军阀。

sentences.en: And then there is this guy, Gilles de Ré, a Breton nobleman with a particular taste for guerrilla warfare.
sentences.zh: 还有这个人，吉尔·德·雷，一位对游击战情有独钟的布列塔尼贵族。

sentences.en: And Guy de Laval knew him very well, because Guy's brother was married to the daughter of Gilles de Ré.
sentences.zh: 盖伊·德·拉瓦尔对他非常了解，因为盖伊的兄弟娶了吉尔·德·雷的女儿。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And there's another side to Gilles de Ré, isn't there, which we perhaps won't go into immediately, but perhaps there's a shadow over his reputation.
sentences.zh: 吉尔·德·雷还有另一面，不是吗？我们或许不会立刻深入探讨，但他的名声上似乎有一层阴影。

sentences.en: We may be coming to that in due course.
sentences.zh: 我们以后可能会谈到这一点。

sentences.en: Anyway, but at the time, there is no blot on the escutcheon of Gilles de Ré or any of the other French captains, because in the wake of the miracle of Orléans,
sentences.zh: 总之，在当时，吉尔·德·雷或其他任何法国将领的声誉上都没有污点，因为在奥尔良奇迹之后，

sentences.en: they have come to think of themselves as brothers in arMs.
sentences.zh: 他们已经把自己视为生死与共的战友。

sentences.en: And they have an incredible glamour now, and this is why Guy de Laval has joined them.
sentences.zh: 他们现在拥有令人难以置信的光环，这就是盖伊·德·拉瓦尔加入他们的原因。

sentences.en: He wants a bit of it himself.
sentences.zh: 他自己也想沾点光。

sentences.en: He wants to join this band of brothers.
sentences.zh: 他想加入这个兄弟会。

sentences.en: However, none of these warlords, none of these captains is the person who most glamorously, most stirringly embodies the miracle of Orléans.
sentences.zh: 然而，这些军阀、这些将领中，没有一个人能像她那样，以最迷人、最激动人心的方式体现奥尔良的奇迹。

sentences.en: It's not the bastard.
sentences.zh: 不是那个私生子。

sentences.en: It's not Laire.
sentences.zh: 不是拉伊尔。

sentences.en: It's not Gilles de Ré.
sentences.zh: 也不是吉尔·德·雷。

sentences.en: It's a teenage girl.
sentences.zh: 而是一个十几岁的女孩。

sentences.en: And the sense of her charisma is palpable in the spirit of devotion with which Guy de Laval has described this person to his mother.
sentences.zh: 盖伊·德·拉瓦尔在写给母亲的信中，那种崇敬之情溢于言表，让人能真切感受到她的人格魅力。

sentences.en: Yes, I saw her mount her horse, arrayed all in white armour, with only her head bare and holding a small axe.
sentences.zh: 是的，我看见她骑上马，身披白甲，只露出头部，手里拿着一把小斧头。

sentences.en: And you can sense here the influence of the kind of Arthurian chivalric romances that were so popular in the 15th century.
sentences.zh: 在这里，你可以感受到15世纪非常流行的亚瑟王骑士传奇的影响。

sentences.en: I mean, she's effectively, it's as though one of the books that they love, one of the stories or the songs that troubadours sing has come to life, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，她实际上就像是他们喜爱的书中人物，或是游吟诗人歌唱的故事，活生生地出现在了现实中，不是吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So this, of course, is Joan of Arc.
sentences.zh: 所以，这当然就是圣女贞德。

sentences.en: And it's absolutely astonishing that only months before, you know, she'd been a peasant in a kind of homespun dress.
sentences.zh: 令人震惊的是，就在几个月前，她还是个穿着粗布衣服的农家女。

sentences.en: And now she is like Sir Lancelot.
sentences.zh: 而现在，她就像兰斯洛特爵士一样。

sentences.en: She's transformed herself into a kind of flower of chivalry.
sentences.zh: 她把自己变成了一朵骑士之花。

sentences.en: And she's won the hearts and the admiration of these very battle-hardened men.
sentences.zh: 她赢得了这些久经沙场的男人们的心和钦佩。

sentences.en: So, you know, the bastard, Laire, Gilles de Ré.
sentences.zh: 你知道，那个私生子、拉伊尔、吉尔·德·雷。

sentences.en: You know, it's astonishing.
sentences.zh: 这真是太令人震惊了。

sentences.en: And she'd done it because she was very courageous.
sentences.zh: 她能做到这一点是因为她非常勇敢。

sentences.en: She'd shown tremendous zeal.
sentences.zh: 她展现出了巨大的热情。

sentences.en: She'd shown enormous, a kind of a real sense of what it would take to defeat the English, to relieve the siege.
sentences.zh: 她展现出了非凡的洞察力，真正明白击败英国人、解除围城需要什么。

sentences.en: But I think also she embodied something that is completely exceptional because Joan of Arc, through the entire sweep of medieval history, is someone exceptional.
sentences.zh: 但我认为她也体现了一些完全特殊的东西，因为在整个中世纪历史长河中，圣女贞德是一个例外。

sentences.en: And this is a kind of instinctive genius for display and image.
sentences.zh: 这是一种对展示和形象把控的本能天赋。

sentences.en: She's kind of the medieval David Bowie on steroids.
sentences.zh: 她简直就是打了兴奋剂的中世纪大卫·鲍伊。

sentences.en: She understands how to project herself.
sentences.zh: 她懂得如何塑造自己。

sentences.en: But just on this, right?
sentences.zh: 但就这一点而言，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, actually, you know, since this is a woman, a sort of Taylor Swift or Lady Gaga might be as good a parallel.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，既然她是一位女性，拿泰勒·斯威夫特或Lady Gaga来类比或许也很恰当。

sentences.en: But just on this, she is drawing not just on the religious iconography and whatnot, but she is very clearly drawing on the tradition of the chivalric romances.
sentences.zh: 但就这一点来说，她不仅是在利用宗教偶像等元素，而且很明显是在借鉴骑士传奇的传统。

sentences.en: And she's playing a part.
sentences.zh: 她在扮演一个角色。

sentences.en: I mean, the point about performance, I think, is really important.
sentences.zh: 我认为关于“表演”这一点非常重要。

sentences.en: She is consciously or unconsciously playing a part that people know will inspire knights and get them excited and all of this sort of stuff.
sentences.zh: 她是有意识或无意识地在扮演一个人们所熟知的角色，这能激励骑士们，让他们感到兴奋，诸如此类。

sentences.en: I mean, there is a definite element of spectacle about the Joan of Arc phenomenon.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，贞德现象中确实存在明显的表演成分。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I mean, I suspect this isn't kind of, you know, calculation.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我怀疑这并非某种算计。

sentences.en: It's expression of what is in her heart.
sentences.zh: 这是她内心的表达。

sentences.en: But what is in her heart has been massively influenced, I think, by the romances that we know that she listened to when she was growing up.
sentences.zh: 但我认为，她内心的东西深受她成长过程中所听到的那些传奇故事的影响。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And clearly she has dreams of chivalry.
sentences.zh: 显然，她有着骑士梦想。

sentences.en: The mad thing is, is that she's not a young man.
sentences.zh: 疯狂的是，她不是个年轻人。

sentences.en: She's a young woman.
sentences.zh: 她是个年轻女性。

sentences.en: She's not only dared to live these dreams out, but she has persuaded hard-bitten noblemen to share in them, to see her, a peasant girl, as a nobleman.
sentences.zh: 她不仅敢于实现这些梦想，还说服了那些硬汉贵族们分享这些梦想，把她这个农家女孩看作一位贵族。

sentences.en: And Marina Warner, whose book I've already cited, is brilliant on this.
sentences.zh: 玛丽娜·华纳，我之前引用过她的书，在这方面写得非常精彩。

sentences.en: So Marina Warner writes, Joan was the personification of mobility.
sentences.zh: 玛丽娜·华纳写道：贞德是流动性的化身。

sentences.en: She accepted neither her peasant birth nor her female condition, none of the limitations society had provided for her circumscription.
sentences.zh: 她既不接受自己的农民出身，也不接受自己的女性身份，更不接受社会强加给她的任何限制。

sentences.en: Instead, in an age of chivalry, she assumed its most successful guise and dressed herself and comported herself like a knight born to the role.
sentences.zh: 相反，在骑士时代，她采用了最成功的装扮，像一位天生的骑士那样穿衣打扮和行事。

sentences.en: But the thing is, of course, she's not a knight.
sentences.zh: 但问题是，她当然不是骑士。

sentences.en: She's a woman.
sentences.zh: 她是女性。

sentences.en: And, I mean, this is the paradox of her, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这就是她身上的悖论，不是吗？

sentences.en: That she's playing a male part, a traditionally male part, and she's surrounded by men.
sentences.zh: 她在扮演一个男性角色，一个传统的男性角色，而且她身边全是男人。

sentences.en: But, I mean, she's not pretending to be a man, right?
sentences.zh: 但我的意思是，她并没有假装自己是男人，对吧？

sentences.en: She doesn't cast off her feminine identity at all.
sentences.zh: 她根本没有抛弃自己的女性身份。

sentences.en: But she actually draws on it.
sentences.zh: 相反，她实际上是在利用它。

sentences.en: And it's the fact that she is, surely that's what gives her part of the sort of, as it were, supernatural or divine power.
sentences.zh: 而且正是因为这一点，才赋予了她某种超自然或神圣的力量，不是吗？

sentences.en: It's the fact that she is setting herself outside the conventional gender norms, no?
sentences.zh: 正是因为她把自己置于传统的性别规范之外，不是吗？

sentences.en: So people see her as a woman apart.
sentences.zh: 所以人们视她为一位超凡的女性。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Or she's fusing the most potent expressions of what is male and female.
sentences.zh: 或者说，她正在融合男性和女性最强大的表现力。

sentences.en: So we've said how, you know, how she's, she buys into the show and the glamour of knighthood.
sentences.zh: 我们已经说过她是如何沉浸在骑士精神的表演和魅力中的。

sentences.en: But she also instinctively understands that there are deep reserves of spiritual power that women particularly are able to channel.
sentences.zh: 但她也本能地理解，女性能够引导出深层的精神力量。

sentences.en: So, you know, she is absolutely not trans.
sentences.zh: 所以，她绝对不是跨性别者。

sentences.en: She does not want to change her sex.
sentences.zh: 她不想改变性别。

sentences.en: She never claims, she never pretends to be male.
sentences.zh: 她从未声称，也从未假装自己是男性。

sentences.en: She always calls herself Jeanne La Pucelle, Joan the Maid.
sentences.zh: 她总是称自己为“贞德，圣女”，即“贞德，少女”。

sentences.en: And what she's doing there is drawing on all the traditions that are associated with the body of a virgin girl.
sentences.zh: 她这样做是在利用与处女之身相关的所有传统。

sentences.en: You know, this, she's casting it as the very essence of her identity.
sentences.zh: 你知道，她将其视为自己身份的核心。

sentences.en: And so she is male in the most martial way.
sentences.zh: 所以，她在武力上是男性化的。

sentences.en: It's possible to be male.
sentences.zh: 这在男性身上是可能的。

sentences.en: But she is female in the holiest way it is possible to be female.
sentences.zh: 但她在女性身份上，又是最神圣的。

sentences.en: And it's this fusion that is so unique and that makes Joan such a completely exceptional person in the, you know, the sweep of medieval European history.
sentences.zh: 正是这种融合如此独特，使得贞德在中世纪欧洲历史的长河中成为一个完全例外的人物。

sentences.en: So we compared her before a couple of times to another person we've done on the show, Catherine of Siena.
sentences.zh: 我们之前曾几次将她与我们在节目中介绍过的另一个人——锡耶纳的凯瑟琳进行比较。

sentences.en: But Catherine of Siena draws almost exclusively on kind of female archetypes.
sentences.zh: 但锡耶纳的凯瑟琳几乎完全借鉴了女性原型。

sentences.en: Well, she's the bride of Christ, isn't she?
sentences.zh: 嗯，她是基督的新娘，不是吗？

sentences.en: Um, Joan is a bit different and in the, in the first episode, you talked about her obsession with St. Michael, the kind of, you know, a patron saint, a warrior saint and so on.
sentences.zh: 嗯，贞德有点不同。在第一集中，你谈到了她对圣迈克尔的痴迷，你知道，那是一位守护圣徒，一位战士圣徒等等。

sentences.en: Um, the captain of heaven, all of that, the leaders of the archangels and St. Michael, I mean, you might say a very male figure, but is he?
sentences.zh: 嗯，天堂的统帅，所有这些，大天使的领袖，圣迈克尔，我的意思是，你可能会说这是一个非常男性化的形象，但真的是吗？

sentences.en: Because he's a little bit amorphous, isn't he?
sentences.zh: 因为他有点无定形，不是吗？

sentences.en: Well, he's, he's an angel and so he's sexless.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他是一位天使，所以他是无性的。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Um, angels do not have sex in any sense.
sentences.zh: 嗯，天使在任何意义上都没有性别。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Well, that's a, that's a very niche, uh, a very niche hobby.
sentences.zh: 好吧，那是一个非常小众的爱好。

sentences.en: And so he's neither male, he's, you know, he's not female.
sentences.zh: 所以他既不是男性，也不是女性。

sentences.en: He is, he is, he's kind of more than that.
sentences.zh: 他，他，他有点超越了这些。

sentences.en: And Michael, as we said, had become the emblem of French resistance and Joan has now become the emblem of French resistance.
sentences.zh: 正如我们所说，迈克尔已成为法国抵抗运动的象征，而贞德现在也成为了法国抵抗运动的象征。

sentences.en: And although the comparison, I don't think is ever overtly made by Joan's contemporaries.
sentences.zh: 虽然我认为贞德的同时代人从未公开进行过这种比较。

sentences.en: There is a hint of this kind of sexless character that they see her as possessing in the way that her companions in arms repeatedly speak of her as someone who is attractive,
sentences.zh: 但在她的战友们反复谈论她时，有一种暗示，认为她拥有某种无性的特质，说她很有吸引力，

sentences.en: but who nevertheless never provokes sexual desire in them.
sentences.zh: 但却从未在他们心中激起过性欲。

sentences.en: So here is, uh, Jean Dolan, her squire, uh, who wrote after, after she had died.
sentences.zh: 所以，这是她的侍从让·多隆在贞德去世后写下的文字。

sentences.en: Although she was a young girl, beautiful and shapely and when helping to arm her or otherwise, I have often seen her breasts.
sentences.zh: “虽然她是个年轻女孩，美丽且身材匀称，在帮她穿盔甲或其他时候，我经常看到她的胸部。”

sentences.en: And although sometimes when I was dressing her wounds, I have seen her legs quite bare and I have gone close to her many times and I was strong, young and vigorous in those days.
sentences.zh: “虽然有时我在为她处理伤口时，看到过她裸露的双腿，而且我曾多次靠近她，那时我年轻力壮，精力充沛。”

sentences.en: Never, despite any sight or contact I had with the maid, was my body moved to any carnal desire for her, nor were any of her soldiers or squired moved in this way.
sentences.zh: “但无论我看到什么或与这位少女有什么接触，我的身体从未对她产生过任何肉欲，她的士兵或侍从们也从未有过这种念头。”

sentences.en: Uh, and I, I think it's important for Joan's comrades, her male comrades, to emphasize that she is a maid,
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为贞德的战友们，她的男性战友们，强调她是“少女”这一点很重要，

sentences.en: that her virginity is the marker of her holiness and that this holiness in turn is the evidence that she is what she says she is, a messenger sent from God.
sentences.zh: 她的贞洁是她神圣性的标志，而这种神圣性反过来又是她是上帝派遣的使者的证据。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And there's no sense that any of the captains at Orléans, you know, when she's berating them and all of that kind of thing,
sentences.zh: 而且，当她在奥尔良训斥那些将领时，诸如此类的事情，

sentences.en: when she is haranguing them about bad decisions and stuff, there's no sense that any of the captains doubt her and say, who is this flipping jumped up peasant girl, you know,
sentences.zh: 当她因为错误的决定而严厉斥责他们时，没有任何将领怀疑她，说“这个突然冒出来的农家女是谁啊”，你知道，

sentences.en: who claims to be sent by God or any of the knights or any of these people that they, they collectively choose to believe.
sentences.zh: 或者质疑她声称是上帝派来的，或者任何骑士或其他人，他们集体选择了相信。

sentences.en: Do they, or are there any skeptics?
sentences.zh: 他们相信吗？还是说有怀疑者？

sentences.en: Of course there are skeptics.
sentences.zh: 当然有怀疑者。

sentences.en: And of course the, it takes time for Joan to persuade them that what she represents is something that they should be buying into, but the proof is in the pudding.
sentences.zh: 当然，贞德需要时间来说服他们，让他们相信她所代表的东西是值得支持的，但事实胜于雄辩。

sentences.en: Um, you know, she prayed, the wind changed.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你知道，她祈祷了，风向就变了。

sentences.en: She suggested that, um, the English should be attacked.
sentences.zh: 她建议应该进攻英国人。

sentences.en: They attack the English.
sentences.zh: 他们就进攻了英国人。

sentences.en: It works out.
sentences.zh: 事情进展得很顺利。

sentences.en: Orléans is liberated.
sentences.zh: 奥尔良解放了。

sentences.en: The miracle stands for itself.
sentences.zh: 奇迹本身就说明了一切。

sentences.en: She's done exactly what she said she would do.
sentences.zh: 她确实做到了她所说的一切。

sentences.en: And this is why people like Guy de Laval, who's kind of enthusiastic description of Joan, we began this show with.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么像居伊·德·拉瓦尔这样的人，会对贞德做出那种充满热情的描述，这也是我们节目开头所提到的。

sentences.en: That's why they're buying into it.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么他们会相信这一点。

sentences.en: You know, it's, there's this electric sense of excitement that everything she had said was true, that God is on the side of French arms,
sentences.zh: 你知道，这是一种令人兴奋的电光火石般的感觉，她所说的一切都是真的，上帝站在法军这一边，

sentences.en: that everything that had seemed terrible has now been raised up in this kind of illumined by this splendor, this sense of glory, this sense of, of kind of, of, of,
sentences.zh: 所有曾经看起来可怕的事情，现在都被这种光辉所照亮，这种荣耀感，这种，这种，这种，

sentences.en: of wonder and the miraculous.
sentences.zh: 这种奇迹般的惊叹感。

sentences.en: And that's what Guy and loads of other people are buying into.
sentences.zh: 这就是居伊和许多其他人所相信的。

sentences.en: I mean, it's, it's interesting because effectively Joan's liberation of Orléans is the only miracle that she has performed.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这很有趣，因为实际上贞德解放奥尔良是她创造的唯一奇迹。

sentences.en: So in that letter that you read, Guy describes how, you know, her horse is a bit frisky and Joan says, take it over to the cross.
sentences.zh: 所以在那封你读过的信里，居伊描述了她的马有点不安，贞德说，把它带到十字架那里去。

sentences.en: And then the horse comes down as though there's a hint of the miraculous there, but I mean, it's pretty feeble stuff.
sentences.zh: 然后马就安静下来了，仿佛其中有一丝奇迹的意味，但我的意思是，这太微不足道了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: You know, visionaries full stop.
sentences.zh: 你知道，空谈的空想家们。

sentences.en: They, they're laying claim to all kinds of miracles.
sentences.zh: 他们声称拥有各种各样的奇迹。

sentences.en: Joan doesn't do that.
sentences.zh: 贞德并没有那样做。

sentences.en: You know, there are, there are lots of people who want her to be a miracle worker, who want her to perform miraculous healings or whatever.
sentences.zh: 你知道，有很多人希望她成为奇迹创造者，希望她能施行奇迹般的治愈或其他什么。

sentences.en: She doesn't.
sentences.zh: 她没有。

sentences.en: Well, even the relief of Orléans.
sentences.zh: 嗯，即使是奥尔良之围的解除。

sentences.en: I mean, it's not really a supernatural miracle.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这并不是真正的超自然奇迹。

sentences.en: I mean, it's, I mean, sieges are often relieved.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，围城战经常会被解除。

sentences.en: I mean, sure, the French thought they were going to lose and actually they ended up winning and they're delighted by that,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，当然，法国人以为他们会输，但实际上他们最终赢了，他们为此感到高兴，

sentences.en: but you don't need to resort to supernatural explanations for why they were able to rout the English.
sentences.zh: 但你不需要诉诸超自然的解释来说明他们为什么能够击溃英国人。

sentences.en: I mean, that's.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，那是。

sentences.en: Well, Dominic, you, you, you, you don't, but that is the, that is the one miracle that Joan says that she has performed.
sentences.zh: 嗯，多米尼克，你，你，你，你不需要，但那确实是贞德声称她创造的唯一奇迹。

sentences.en: And I guess you would say it was a miracle that the relief of Orléans was performed by a peasant girl.
sentences.zh: 我想你会说，由一个农家少女来解除奥尔良之围本身就是一个奇迹。

sentences.en: I mean, that does seem really stunning and people buy into the fact that that is properly miraculous,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这看起来确实非常令人震惊，人们相信这确实是奇迹，

sentences.en: but there isn't really anything else because Joan wants the focus to be entirely on the mission that she has been given by her voices.
sentences.zh: 但除此之外并没有什么别的了，因为贞德希望人们完全专注于她从声音中得到的使命。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And that mission was to relieve Orléans and that was the test and she has passed it.
sentences.zh: 而那个使命就是解除奥尔良之围，那是对她的考验，她通过了。

sentences.en: And so her claim to have been sent from God is now widely accepted by basically everyone on the French side.
sentences.zh: 所以她声称自己是上帝派来的，现在基本上被法国这边的所有人广泛接受了。

sentences.en: Not least the man that she is serving, who is the Dauphin.
sentences.zh: 尤其是她所效忠的那个人，也就是王储。

sentences.en: So even Joan still calls him the Dauphin, don't they?
sentences.zh: 所以即使是贞德也还称他为王储，不是吗？

sentences.en: Everybody calls him the Dauphin, you know, the titular Charles VII, because he won't really become king or be accepted as king.
sentences.zh: 每个人都称他为王储，你知道，名义上的查理七世，因为他还没有真正成为国王，也没有被承认为国王。

sentences.en: So he's driven back the English and gone into Reims and been crowned because Reims, 80 miles northeast of Paris in English held territory.
sentences.zh: 所以他击退了英国人，进入兰斯并加冕，因为兰斯位于巴黎东北80英里处的英占领土上。

sentences.en: This is the place where for generations, French kings have been crowned.
sentences.zh: 这是几代法国国王加冕的地方。

sentences.en: Millennium.
sentences.zh: 千年以来皆是如此。

sentences.en: You need to get there.
sentences.zh: 你必须到达那里。

sentences.en: And Charles has been hanging around for seven years since the death of his father in 1422, hoping desperately he can get to Reims and be crowned.
sentences.zh: 查理自1422年他父亲去世以来，已经徘徊了七年，绝望地希望他能到达兰斯并加冕。

sentences.en: And there seems no prospect of it whatsoever.
sentences.zh: 而且看起来根本没有任何希望。

sentences.en: And Joan has promised him not only that she will relieve Orléans, but that she will crown him in Reims and drive out the English with him.
sentences.zh: 贞德不仅向他保证她会解除奥尔良之围，还会让他在兰斯加冕，并与他一起驱逐英国人。

sentences.en: So he must now be thinking, well, she's done number one.
sentences.zh: 所以他现在一定在想，好吧，她完成了第一项。

sentences.en: What about number two and number three?
sentences.zh: 第二项和第三项呢？

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 是的，绝对是。

sentences.en: And in the weeks that follow the relief of Orléans, he kind of really sets his shoulder to the wheel in an attempt to try and help her fulfill these other two prophecies.
sentences.zh: 在奥尔良之围解除后的几周里，他确实全力以赴，试图帮助她实现另外两个预言。

sentences.en: So the relief force that had been sent to Orléans, that had been disbanded almost immediately after the relief of the city,
sentences.zh: 所以那支被派往奥尔良的救援部队，在城市解围后几乎立即解散了，

sentences.en: basically because there aren't any funds left to keep it in the field.
sentences.zh: 基本上是因为没有资金维持他们在前线了。

sentences.en: The Dauphin's treasury is empty.
sentences.zh: 王储的国库空空如也。

sentences.en: And that, again, is part of the miraculous quality of the relief of Orléans.
sentences.zh: 而这，再次成为奥尔良之围奇迹的一部分。

sentences.en: Or, you know, it's come despite the fact that the Dauphin effectively is bankrupt.
sentences.zh: 或者说，你知道，尽管王储实际上已经破产了，但它还是发生了。

sentences.en: In the wake of the relief of Orléans, the Dauphin is now confident that men will answer his call and not expect to be paid.
sentences.zh: 在奥尔良之围解除后，王储现在确信人们会响应他的号召，而不指望得到报酬。

sentences.en: Because now they will do it because, you know, they are following a miraculous virgin.
sentences.zh: 因为现在他们会这样做，因为，你知道，他们是在追随一位奇迹般的圣女。

sentences.en: God, that really would be a miracle if they want to fight and not be paid.
sentences.zh: 天哪，如果他们愿意战斗而不拿报酬，那才真是个奇迹。

sentences.en: That is what turns out to be the case, because by early June, some 5,000 men have assembled at Cels, which is this small town south of the Loire, between Tours and Orléans.
sentences.zh: 事实证明确实如此，因为到六月初，大约5000人聚集在塞尔，这是卢瓦尔河以南，图尔和奥尔良之间的一个小镇。

sentences.en: And among them, of course, was Guy de Laval.
sentences.zh: 当然，其中就有居伊·德·拉瓦尔。

sentences.en: So he's kind of typical of, you know,
sentences.zh: 所以他算是，你知道，

sentences.en: he's expressive of why these people are now ready to fight for the Dauphin in a way that they hadn't been before and not expect to be paid for it.
sentences.zh: 他表达了为什么这些人现在愿意以一种以前没有过的方式为王储而战，并且不指望得到报酬。

sentences.en: And in fact, Guy de Laval, to fund this campaigning, he had been forced to sell lands.
sentences.zh: 事实上，居伊·德·拉瓦尔为了资助这次战役，被迫变卖了土地。

sentences.en: So not only is he not being paid, he's actually, you know, he's short of a few estates or two.
sentences.zh: 所以他不仅没有得到报酬，实际上，你知道，他还少了几个庄园。

sentences.en: Now, among the various nobles and captains of France, as we mentioned in the previous episode, there is one who, right from the beginning, has been a massive Joan fan.
sentences.zh: 现在，在法国的各种贵族和将领中，正如我们在上一集提到的，有一个人从一开始就是贞德的铁杆粉丝。

sentences.en: And this is the Duke of Alençon, Jean, who's only 20, but has been appointed by the Dauphin to serve as commander in chief of this expeditionary force that has been recruited.
sentences.zh: 这就是阿朗松公爵让，他才20岁，但被王储任命为这支招募的远征军的总司令。

sentences.en: Joan herself, even though in her letters she described herself as a captain of men, she has no official rank, but she doesn't actually need one.
sentences.zh: 贞德本人，尽管她在信中称自己为军队统帅，但她没有正式军衔，但她实际上并不需要。

sentences.en: And the Dauphin gives instructions to Alençon that he is to act in all matters by her advice.
sentences.zh: 王储指示阿朗松，在所有事务上都要听从她的建议。

sentences.en: And as it turns out, the campaign is an amazing success.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，这次战役取得了惊人的成功。

sentences.en: And Joan's advice, again, turns out to be incredibly effective.
sentences.zh: 而贞德的建议，再次证明是非常有效的。

sentences.en: And just as they had been humiliated at Orléans, so now a succession of English commanders find themselves very much coming second best when they come up against Joan and her men.
sentences.zh: 就像他们在奥尔良受到羞辱一样，现在一系列英国指挥官在面对贞德和她的士兵时，发现自己处于下风。

sentences.en: So let's, should we go through these campaigns?
sentences.zh: 那么，我们来回顾一下这些战役好吗？

sentences.en: So first of all, there's a place called Jardot, and that's upriver from Orléans.
sentences.zh: 首先，有一个叫雅尔若的地方，在奥尔良的上游。

sentences.en: It's a bridging point.
sentences.zh: 那是一个桥头堡。

sentences.en: The Duke of Suffolk is there, and he's there, and his men are completely battered by French artillery, aren't they?
sentences.zh: 萨福克公爵在那里，他的士兵被法国炮兵彻底击溃了，不是吗？

sentences.en: The French have a bombard called the Shepherdess, which is named after Joan.
sentences.zh: 法国人有一门叫“牧羊女”的臼炮，是以贞德的名字命名的。

sentences.en: And, you know, the artillery does its work, the keep collapses, and then Joan and co.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，炮兵发挥了作用，堡垒倒塌了，然后贞德和同伴们

sentences.en: storm the city walls.
sentences.zh: 冲进了城墙。

sentences.en: She's waving her banner, fight hard, and God will fight hard with you.
sentences.zh: 她挥舞着旗帜，奋勇战斗，上帝会与你们并肩作战。

sentences.en: God has doomed the English.
sentences.zh: 上帝已经注定了英国人的灭亡。

sentences.en: And the English end up being taken prisoner, including the Duke of Suffolk.
sentences.zh: 英国人最终被俘虏，包括萨福克公爵。

sentences.en: So that's a massive blow for the English.
sentences.zh: 这对英国人来说是一个巨大的打击。

sentences.en: And the Duke of Suffolk behaves splendidly, doesn't he?
sentences.zh: 萨福克公爵表现得非常出色，不是吗？

sentences.en: He does.
sentences.zh: 确实。

sentences.en: Sportingly.
sentences.zh: 很有风度。

sentences.en: He knights the person who takes him prisoner, which I think is tremendous.
sentences.zh: 他授予俘虏他的人骑士爵位，我认为这太了不起了。

sentences.en: Or you might say snobbishly, because he doesn't want to be captured by someone who's not a knight.
sentences.zh: 或者你也可以说他很势利，因为他不想被一个不是骑士的人俘虏。

sentences.en: Yeah, so that's the Duke of Suffolk taken prisoner.
sentences.zh: 是的，这就是被俘的萨福克公爵。

sentences.en: And he, of course, had been in command at Orléans.
sentences.zh: 当然，他曾是奥尔良的指挥官。

sentences.en: But one week later, there's an even more crushing blow for the English to endure,
sentences.zh: 但一周后，英国人又遭受了更沉重的打击，

sentences.en: because this time it's the turn of Talbot, Sir John Talbot, the great Lawrence Delaglio of the English, to be taken prisoner.
sentences.zh: 因为这次轮到塔尔博特，约翰·塔尔博特爵士，英国人的劳伦斯·德拉利奥，被俘虏了。

sentences.en: And he suffers a crushing defeat, not in, you know, he's not defending a town.
sentences.zh: 他遭受了惨败，不是在，你知道，他不是在防守城镇。

sentences.en: He's in the open.
sentences.zh: 他在开阔地带。

sentences.en: And this is a pitched battle of the kind that the English, ever since Agincourt, have pretty much taken for granted that they are bound to win.
sentences.zh: 这是一场自阿金库尔战役以来，英国人一直认为他们注定会赢的那种正面交锋。

sentences.en: But now they lose.
sentences.zh: 但现在他们输了。

sentences.en: 2,000 Englishmen are killed.
sentences.zh: 2000名英国人被杀。

sentences.en: You know, this is a loss of manpower that they can't really afford.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这是他们无法承受的人力损失。

sentences.en: But, of course, even more damagingly, perhaps, is the fact that they have lost this reputation for invincibility.
sentences.zh: 但当然，也许更具破坏性的是，他们失去了不可战胜的声誉。

sentences.en: And again, you know, this redounds massively to Joan's credit.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，这极大地归功于贞德。

sentences.en: And she goes to the Dauphin and she says, look, we've had these twin victories.
sentences.zh: 她去找王储说，看，我们取得了这两场胜利。

sentences.en: Two of your enemies are now prisoner, Suffolk and Talbot.
sentences.zh: 你的两个敌人现在是俘虏，萨福克和塔尔博特。

sentences.en: God is clearly with you.
sentences.zh: 上帝显然与你同在。

sentences.en: Now, we must seize the moment.
sentences.zh: 现在，我们必须抓住时机。

sentences.en: We must advance beyond the safe zone of the Loire and we must go deep into enemy-held territory.
sentences.zh: 我们必须推进到卢瓦尔河的安全区之外，深入敌占区。

sentences.en: And our target must be a place some 130 miles to the north of the Loire, beyond Paris.
sentences.zh: 我们的目标必须是卢瓦尔河以北约130英里处，巴黎之外的一个地方。

sentences.en: And this is, of course, the holy city of France.
sentences.zh: 当然，这就是法国的圣城。

sentences.en: And this is a really, really sort of dodgy undertaking for a couple of reasons.
sentences.zh: 由于几个原因，这确实是一个非常冒险的举动。

sentences.en: First of all, you know, it's 130 miles away.
sentences.zh: 首先，你知道，它在130英里之外。

sentences.en: They're not going to have time to organize a supply train.
sentences.zh: 他们没有时间组织补给车队。

sentences.en: They're going to have to move very fast for that reason.
sentences.zh: 因此，他们必须快速移动。

sentences.en: And because of that, because they're not going to be able to take supplies, they are not going to be able to take artillery either,

sentences.en: Everyone in that battle, Burgundian as well as French, absolutely knows who she is.
sentences.zh: 战场上的每一个人，无论是勃艮第人还是法国人，都绝对知道她是谁。

sentences.en: So eventually she heads back towards the drawbridge, towards the gate.
sentences.zh: 所以最终她向吊桥和城门方向撤退。

sentences.en: But by now, the guards in Compiègne are worried that the Burgundians will break in if they leave it open.
sentences.zh: 但此时，贡比涅的守卫担心如果他们敞开大门，勃艮第人会冲进来。

sentences.en: So very reluctantly, they close the gates and they pull up the drawbridge.
sentences.zh: 所以他们非常不情愿地关上了城门，拉起了吊桥。

sentences.en: And Joan is now stuck on the wrong side of the moat.
sentences.zh: 而贞德现在被困在了护城河的另一边。

sentences.en: And so she's surrounded by a swarm of Burgundian soldiers.
sentences.zh: 她被一群勃艮第士兵包围了。

sentences.en: She's pulled down from her horse.
sentences.zh: 她被从马上拽了下来。

sentences.en: She rises to her feet.
sentences.zh: 她站起身来。

sentences.en: She draws her sword.
sentences.zh: 她拔出了剑。

sentences.en: She looks around for a suitable person to surrender to.
sentences.zh: 她环顾四周，寻找一个合适的人投降。

sentences.en: There's a Burgundian captain.
sentences.zh: 那里有一位勃艮第队长。

sentences.en: And she hands the sword over to him.
sentences.zh: 她把剑交给了他。

sentences.en: And Jean LaPucelle is now a prisoner.
sentences.zh: 圣女贞德现在成了俘虏。

sentences.en: So Philip the Good, the Duke of Burgundy, must be absolutely delighted.
sentences.zh: 那么，勃艮第公爵好人菲利普一定非常高兴吧。

sentences.en: Yeah, so we have a witness who sees him.
sentences.zh: 是的，我们有一位目击者看到了他。

sentences.en: He comes to inspect Joan.
sentences.zh: 他来视察贞德。

sentences.en: And the witness says, I've never seen anyone so delighted.
sentences.zh: 目击者说，我从未见过如此高兴的人。

sentences.en: And that evening, after the Duke of Burgundy has been to look at Joan, he writes letters
sentences.zh: 那天晚上，勃艮第公爵看过贞德之后，他写信给法国和低地国家的所有城镇，

sentences.en: to all the towns in France and the Low Countries who might have been tempted to rebel against him.
sentences.zh: 那些可能曾想过反抗他的城镇。

sentences.en: And he proclaims, you know, this glorious achievement.
sentences.zh: 他宣扬了，你知道，这一辉煌的成就。

sentences.en: Joan's capture, we are certain, will everywhere be greeted as the most splendid news, for it clearly
sentences.zh: 我们确信，贞德被俘的消息在各地都会被视为最棒的新闻，因为它清楚地

sentences.en: demonstrates the error and foolish credulity of all those who have let themselves be convinced by the deeds of this woman.
sentences.zh: 证明了所有那些被这个女人的事迹所说服的人的错误和愚蠢的轻信。

sentences.en: And as it turns out, Joan's capture is a servant of a particularly proficient Burgundian lord,
sentences.zh: 事实证明，贞德的俘虏是一位特别能干的勃艮第领主的仆人，

sentences.en: a very loyal servant, not just of the Duke of Burgundy himself, but of Bedford and the
sentences.zh: 一个非常忠诚的仆人，不仅是对勃艮第公爵本人，而且对贝德福德和

sentences.en: English cause.
sentences.zh: 英国事业也是如此。

sentences.en: And this is, he's called John of Luxembourg.
sentences.zh: 他叫卢森堡的约翰。

sentences.en: He has a, you know, he's, he's a very serious player, a very loyal servant of the Anglo-Burgundian alliance.
sentences.zh: 他是一个，你知道，他是一个非常重要的人物，是英勃联盟非常忠诚的仆人。

sentences.en: And so this is the person into whose hands Joan now passes.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是贞德现在落入其手中的人。

sentences.en: And Joan, of course, absolutely, you know, she sees herself as a knight.
sentences.zh: 当然，贞德绝对，你知道，她把自己视为一名骑士。

sentences.en: She is of now of noble standing.
sentences.zh: 她现在拥有高贵的地位。

sentences.en: She sees herself, therefore, as a prisoner of war, whose treatment should be governed by the laws of war.
sentences.zh: 因此，她认为自己是一名战俘，其待遇应受战争法管辖。

sentences.en: And John of Luxembourg is not reluctant to buy into this, because, of course, if Joan is a prisoner of war, is of noble standing, then he stands to make a lot of money, huge
sentences.zh: 而卢森堡的约翰并不排斥这一点，因为当然，如果贞德是战俘，拥有高贵地位，那么他就能赚很多钱，获得巨大的

sentences.en: profit.
sentences.zh: 利润。

sentences.en: He can ransom her or sell her on for a large sum.
sentences.zh: 他可以勒索赎金或以高价把她卖掉。

sentences.en: But there are complications with this.
sentences.zh: 但这其中有复杂的情况。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Because who's going to pay this ransom, right?
sentences.zh: 因为谁会支付这笔赎金呢，对吧？

sentences.en: Well, you would think the obvious person is the man whose cause she has promoted for so long, who is Charles VII of France.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你会认为最明显的人选就是她长期支持其事业的那个人，也就是法国的查理七世。

sentences.en: But disappointingly, Charles VII.
sentences.zh: 但令人失望的是，查理七世。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: He, I reckon, you see, I reckon there's a part of him that thinks, oh, thank God I've got rid of that.
sentences.zh: 我想，你看，我想他心里有一部分在想，哦，谢天谢地，我终于摆脱那个麻烦了。

sentences.en: You know, she was becoming a bit of an albatross.
sentences.zh: 你知道，她正变得像个累赘。

sentences.en: A bit of a nightmare.
sentences.zh: 简直是一场噩梦。

sentences.en: Yeah, a bit of a nightmare.
sentences.zh: 没错，简直是一场噩梦。

sentences.en: I'm kind of glad that they've got her now and I don't want her back.
sentences.zh: 我很高兴他们现在抓住了她，我不想让她回来。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And I think also the fact that Joan has been captured is also potentially very, very damaging.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为贞德被俘的事实也可能具有非常非常大的破坏性。

sentences.en: And so Charles doesn't comment on it.
sentences.zh: 所以查理对此不予置评。

sentences.en: He never mentions Joan by word from this point on.
sentences.zh: 从这一点开始，他再也没有提过贞德的名字。

sentences.en: And instead, he hands over responsibility for the crisis to his chancellor, who is the
sentences.zh: 相反，他把处理危机的责任交给了他的大臣，也就是

sentences.en: Archbishop of Rance, who had crowned him.
sentences.zh: 为他加冕的兰斯大主教。

sentences.en: And the Archbishop of Rance, who was also the guy who had led the investigation into Joan back in Poitiers before the Siege of Orleans, he now basically operates as Charles' spin
sentences.zh: 而兰斯大主教，也就是在奥尔良之围前在普瓦捷主持对贞德调查的那个人，现在基本上充当了查理的公关

sentences.en: doctor.
sentences.zh: 专家。

sentences.en: And his take on Joan is that she'd gone rogue and that although her mission had indeed been blessed by God, she'd gone so off-piste that she has now been undone by her own pride
sentences.zh: 他对贞德的看法是，她已经失控了，虽然她的使命确实得到了上帝的祝福，但她走得太偏了，现在被她自己的骄傲和愚蠢所毁灭。

sentences.en: and folly.
sentences.zh: 因此，上帝通过允许她被俘来惩罚她。

sentences.en: And God has therefore punished her by allowing her to be captured.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，就是这样。

sentences.en: And therefore, you know, that's it.
sentences.zh: 上帝基本上已经不再管她了。

sentences.en: God's washed his hands of her, basically.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你不需要非常愤世嫉俗也能相信这一点，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, you don't have to be incredibly cynical to believe that, though, do you?
sentences.zh: 因为如果你相信她之前的成功是上帝的祝福，那么当事情出错时，

sentences.en: Because if you believe that her previous success was blessed by God, when things go wrong,
sentences.zh: 那肯定表明她误解了上帝的意愿，上帝已经抛弃了她。

sentences.en: that shows that she's misunderstood God's wishes and that God has abandoned her, surely.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以很真诚地这样想。

sentences.en: So you could think that quite sincerely.
sentences.zh: 我想你绝对可以，但显而易见，这位曾赞助查理七世加冕礼的人现在明显未能保持上帝的恩宠，这确实令人尴尬。

sentences.en: I think you absolutely could, but it is obviously an embarrassment that this person who had sponsored
sentences.zh: 所以我认为查理的意思是，我们还是保持沉默吧。

sentences.en: the coronation of Charles VII has now demonstrably failed to maintain the favour of God.
sentences.zh: 我们就假装这件事从未发生过。

sentences.en: So I think in Charles' opinion, let's just keep quiet about it.
sentences.zh: 我们只希望整件事能烟消云散。

sentences.en: Let's just pretend it never happened.
sentences.zh: 现在，它不会烟消云散，因为当然，贝德福德公爵的目标恰恰相反。

sentences.en: Let's just hope the whole business will go away.
sentences.zh: 他想尽可能地大肆宣扬贞德被俘的消息。

sentences.en: Now, it's not going to go away because, of course, the goal of the Duke of Bedford is the precise opposite.
sentences.zh: 我认为他觉得贞德被俘给了他一个机会，可以从失败的边缘夺取一场绝对震撼的宣传胜利。

sentences.en: He wants to make as big a fuss of Jones' capture as he possibly can.
sentences.zh: 他想尽可能地把琼斯的被捕闹得沸沸扬扬。

sentences.en: And I think that he feels that Jones' capture has given him the opportunity to pluck from the very jaws of defeat an absolutely seismic propaganda victory.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为他觉得琼斯的被捕让他有机会从失败的边缘，攫取一场极其震撼的宣传胜利。

sentences.en: What he needs to do is basically so tarnish the coronation of Charles VII that people go back to saying he's an illegitimate king.
sentences.zh: 他需要做的基本上就是玷污查理七世的加冕礼，让人们重新开始说他是个非法国王。

sentences.en: And so Bedford, by now, is adopting a two-pronged strategy to bring this about.
sentences.zh: 因此，贝德福德公爵此时正采取双管齐下的策略来实现这一目标。

sentences.en: Firstly, the month before Jones' capture, he had sent for the eight-year-old Henry VI to come to Calais.
sentences.zh: 首先，在琼被俘的前一个月，他已经派人去加来接八岁的亨利六世。

sentences.en: And Bedford's plan is to have him crowned in Reims or at a pinch Paris and thereby erase the memory of
sentences.zh: 贝德福德的计划是让他能在兰斯，或者退而求其次在巴黎加冕，从而抹去人们对

sentences.en: Charles' coronation.
sentences.zh: 查理加冕礼的记忆。

sentences.en: This is his plan.
sentences.zh: 这就是他的计划。

sentences.en: There is a problem.
sentences.zh: 但有一个问题。

sentences.en: Reims is still in enemy hands and Normandy is too unstable to risk the king travelling to Paris.
sentences.zh: 兰斯仍处于敌手，而诺曼底局势太不稳定，无法冒险让国王前往巴黎。

sentences.en: So it's a bit like, you know, in the wake of the Iraq war, President Bush, you know, he could maybe land in
sentences.zh: 所以这有点像，你知道，伊拉克战争之后，布什总统，你知道，他或许能降落在

sentences.en: Baghdad and stay in the green zone, but he couldn't venture out to Fallujah.
sentences.zh: 巴格达并待在绿区，但他不敢冒险去费卢杰。

sentences.en: There's the same issue with, you know, they can't guarantee Henry VI's safety.
sentences.zh: 他们面临着同样的问题，你知道，他们无法保证亨利六世的安全。

sentences.en: And so instead, he's left to kick his heels in Calais and it's all a bit embarrassing.
sentences.zh: 所以他只能在加来干等，这实在有点尴尬。

sentences.en: And then suddenly, Joan is captured and now Bedford can see a second massive opportunity.
sentences.zh: 然后突然间，琼被俘了，贝德福德现在看到了第二个巨大的机会。

sentences.en: The witch is in the hands of one of his allies.
sentences.zh: 这个女巫落入了他的一位盟友手中。

sentences.en: And it is Pierre Cochon, the Bishop of Beauvais, within whose bishopric, crucially, Joan had been captured,
sentences.zh: 而皮埃尔·科雄，博韦的主教，关键在于琼正是在他的教区内被捕的，

sentences.en: who now steps up to the plate with a solution that he presents to Bedford.
sentences.zh: 他现在挺身而出，向贝德福德提出了一个解决方案。

sentences.en: And he says to Bedford, look, you should buy Joan off John of Luxembourg.
sentences.zh: 他对贝德福德说，听着，你应该从卢森堡的约翰手中买下琼。

sentences.en: And then when Joan is in the hands of the English, hand her over to us, to the church.
sentences.zh: 然后当琼落入英国人手中时，把她交给我们，交给教会。

sentences.en: And I, in my role as Bishop of Beauvais, will try her for heresy, for sorcery, for conjuring up demons, basically for anything you want to mention.
sentences.zh: 而我，作为博韦主教，将以异端、巫术、召唤恶魔的罪名审判她，基本上就是你想得到的任何罪名。

sentences.en: I can guarantee, because I know that she's a witch, that she will be convicted.
sentences.zh: 我可以保证，因为我知道她是女巫，她一定会被定罪。

sentences.en: And when she is convicted, then the coronation of the Dauphin will be revealed to the world to have been a literally satanic fraud.
sentences.zh: 当她被定罪后，王储的加冕礼就会向世人揭示，那简直是一场撒旦式的骗局。

sentences.en: Just one quick point.
sentences.zh: 提个小点。

sentences.en: Again, is this cynicism?
sentences.zh: 再说一次，这是愤世嫉俗吗？

sentences.en: Is this cynical policy?
sentences.zh: 这是愤世嫉俗的政策吗？

sentences.en: No, it's not cynicism at all.
sentences.zh: 不，这完全不是愤世嫉俗。

sentences.en: He genuinely, like, I think this is important to get across to people, because I think there's
sentences.zh: 他是真诚的，就像，我认为这一点对人们来说很重要，因为我认为有一种

sentences.en: a general perception that, oh, this was terribly manipulative and cynical, the trial of Joan and all this.
sentences.zh: 普遍的看法，噢，这太具操纵性和愤世嫉俗了，对琼的审判以及所有这些。

sentences.en: But the English genuinely, genuinely, sincerely think this woman quite clearly is a witch.
sentences.zh: 但英国人确实、确实、真诚地认为这个女人很明显就是个女巫。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And the French servants of the Lancastrian regime think that as well.
sentences.zh: 兰开斯特政权的法国仆从们也这么认为。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Of course, I mean, that conviction is interfused with a desire to preserve the regime that they have committed themselves to serving.
sentences.zh: 当然，我的意思是，这种信念与维护他们承诺效忠的政权的愿望交织在一起。

sentences.en: I mean, there's no question about that.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这一点毫无疑问。

sentences.en: But it's perfectly possible to believe that your own interests and the interests of God are one and the same.
sentences.zh: 但完全有可能相信你自己的利益和上帝的利益是同一回事。

sentences.en: I'm glad that we've proved the sincerity of the English.
sentences.zh: 我很高兴我们证明了英国人的诚意。

sentences.en: Let's continue.
sentences.zh: 让我们继续。

sentences.en: So this strikes Bedford as a brilliant plan.
sentences.zh: 所以这让贝德福德觉得是个绝妙的计划。

sentences.en: Basically, everyone's a winner.
sentences.zh: 基本上，每个人都是赢家。

sentences.en: John of Luxembourg is going to get his money.
sentences.zh: 卢森堡的约翰将得到他的钱。

sentences.en: The English are going to get their hands on the witch who has done their cause such lethal harm.
sentences.zh: 英国人将抓到那个给他们的事业造成如此致命伤害的女巫。

sentences.en: And the Bishop of Beauvais has the opportunity to serve the Lord, his God, by getting rid of a witch.
sentences.zh: 而博韦主教有机会通过除掉一个女巫来侍奉他的上帝。

sentences.en: Brilliant.
sentences.zh: 绝妙。

sentences.en: So brilliant.
sentences.zh: 太绝妙了。

sentences.en: Everyone wins.
sentences.zh: 每个人都赢了。

sentences.en: The only person who doesn't win, of course, is Joan.
sentences.zh: 当然，唯一没赢的人就是琼。

sentences.en: And she, when she is informed that she is going to be sold to the English, hurls herself from the window of the 60-foot tower in which John of Luxembourg has been keeping her.
sentences.zh: 当她被告知将被卖给英国人时，她从卢森堡的约翰关押她的那座60英尺高的塔楼窗户跳了下去。

sentences.en: Oh, my God.
sentences.zh: 噢，天哪。

sentences.en: 60 feet.
sentences.zh: 60英尺。

sentences.en: I know.
sentences.zh: 我知道。

sentences.en: It's incredible.
sentences.zh: 这太不可思议了。

sentences.en: Somehow she survives the fall.
sentences.zh: 不知何故，她从坠落中幸存了下来。

sentences.en: I mean, something must have broken it.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，一定有什么东西缓冲了它。

sentences.en: But she's very badly concussed.
sentences.zh: 但她脑震荡非常严重。

sentences.en: You know, I think she does damage to her liver.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我想她的肝脏受损了。

sentences.en: She's obviously badly injured.
sentences.zh: 她显然伤得很重。

sentences.en: And so it takes time for her to be nursed back to health.
sentences.zh: 所以她需要时间来调养恢复健康。

sentences.en: But, you know, the deal has been done.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，交易已经达成了。

sentences.en: And so Bedford can think, brilliant.
sentences.zh: 所以贝德福德可以想，太棒了。

sentences.en: Now, at last, we have a plan.
sentences.zh: 现在，终于，我们有了一个计划。

sentences.en: So by July, suficients in Normandy have sufficiently stabilized that Henry VI can now process from
sentences.zh: 到了七月，诺曼底的局势已经足够稳定，亨利六世现在可以从

sentences.en: Calais to Rouen.
sentences.zh: 加来前往鲁昂。

sentences.en: And Rouen, which is the leading city in Normandy, by this point, well, it is effectively the kind of the green zone for the English regime.
sentences.zh: 而鲁昂，作为诺曼底的主要城市，到此时，嗯，它实际上就是英国政权的绿区。

sentences.en: It's the place that is absolutely secure.
sentences.zh: 那是绝对安全的地方。

sentences.en: It is the Lancastrian stronghold.
sentences.zh: 它是兰开斯特的据点。

sentences.en: And so Henry arrives there and Bedford and the Lancastrian regime can be confident that he is safe and secure there.
sentences.zh: 所以亨利抵达那里，贝德福德和兰开斯特政权可以确信他在那里是安全无虞的。

sentences.en: Then in September, Joan is formally delivered by John of Luxembourg to the English.
sentences.zh: 然后在九月，琼被卢森堡的约翰正式移交给英国人。

sentences.en: He gets a massive payment.
sentences.zh: 他得到了一笔巨额报酬。

sentences.en: He's very happy about that.
sentences.zh: 他对此非常高兴。

sentences.en: That November, Joan is taken to a fortress in the mouth of the Seine, while a military escort is recruited to escort her to Rouen.
sentences.zh: 那年十一月，琼被带到塞纳河口的一座堡垒，同时招募了一支军事护卫队护送她去鲁昂。

sentences.en: And finally, on the 23rd of December, so just before Christmas, she's under very heavy guard.
sentences.zh: 最后，在12月23日，也就是圣诞节前夕，她在严密的看守下。

sentences.en: She's loaded down with chains.
sentences.zh: 她身上戴着沉重的锁链。

sentences.en: She is brought through the gates into Rouen, a city she is destined never to leave because, of course, Dominic, she has less than half a year to live.
sentences.zh: 她被带过城门进入鲁昂，这座她注定永远无法离开的城市，因为，多米尼克，她只剩下不到半年的生命了。

sentences.en: Crikey.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: Well, just one episode to go to complete the story of Joan of Arc.
sentences.zh: 好吧，只剩下一集就能讲完圣女贞德的故事了。

sentences.en: And if you really can't wait, as I can't wait, then if you're a member of the Rest is History
